facts.statement: The Python 3.12 asyncio.wait_for documentation states that a timeout cancels the task and raises the built-in TimeoutError; its example catches TimeoutError.
The Python 3.10 asyncio.wait_for documentation states that a timeout cancels the task and raises asyncio.TimeoutError, and its example catches asyncio.TimeoutError.
The Python 3.12 asyncio exceptions documentation describes asyncio.TimeoutError as a deprecated alias of the built-in TimeoutError and records that it became an alias in Python 3.11.

findings.statement: The apparent exception-name conflict is version-dependent: Python 3.10 documentation uses asyncio.TimeoutError, while Python 3.12 documentation uses built-in TimeoutError for asyncio.wait_for.
For Python 3.12, the two names refer to the same exception class because asyncio.TimeoutError is documented as an alias of TimeoutError; the older spelling is nevertheless documented as deprecated.
The sources support a specific timeout-exception handler for the stated Python 3.12 scope; they do not support broadening this path to catch Exception merely to hide the version distinction.

uncertainties.statement: The fixture establishes Python 3.12 as the deployed target but does not establish whether the project also supports interpreters before Python 3.11; the exact provenance and revision of the older document mentioned in the local review note are also unavailable.

proposals.statement: For code scoped to Python 3.12, use the built-in TimeoutError in the asyncio.wait_for handler and keep the handler specific. If pre-3.11 interpreters must also be supported, resolve that compatibility requirement before applying a cross-version repair.
